thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert: cross-region routing anomalies detected for region steering policy 'latency-steer-v2'. Threshold breached for 3+ vanity routes in ap-northeast-1 -> eu-west-2 path. Alert ID: RE-INF-2026-4721

Aisha (infra-oncall): I'm on it. seeing ~1200ms p50 for requests pinned to eu-west-2 from ap-northeast-1, and error rate bump to 3.2%. Spread looks concentrated to a subset of pinned routes.

Marco (netops): Confirmed. BGP next-hops show normal, but our routing control plane applied an unintended weight change during a config push at 03:12 UTC. Suspect policy engine mis-evaluated latency metric window.

Leah (duty-sre): Can we roll back the policy? Which commit/ID caused the change?

Marco (netops): Rollback candidate is: commit 7b9f2c3 (latency-steer: change smoothing window from 120s -> 30s). I can revert the policy in the controller. Reverting should push a diff to route-propagator and re-evaluate weights.

Ravi (eng-runtime): Heads-up: if we change weights aggressively we may cause cache misses on KV prefixes and a small spike in tail latency. Plan: revert weight change, keep reduced concurrency for 30s, then gradually lift.

Julia (support-lead): Customer impact check: Support dashboards show 14 active customer sessions with degraded returns tied to the eu-west-2 model backends. Notifying top 3 paying customers now. @customer-advocate will draft comms.

customer-advocate: Draft sent to #customer-comms-draft for review. No public page yet. ETA 10m.

Aisha (infra-oncall): Action plan: 1) netops revert policy to commit 7a4d1ee (pre-change) 2) runtime throttle non-critical background inference in eu-west-2 3) flush route cache at edge proxies for affected prefixes 4) monitor for 5m before full lift.

Marco (netops): Running rollback now:

```
# rollback steering policy
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood-inference.internal/api/policies/latency-steer-v2/rollback" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"target_commit":"7a4d1ee","reason":"incident RE-INF-2026-4721 - revert smoothing window change"}'
```

Marco (netops): 03:25 UTC -> rollback accepted by controller, propagating diffs to region controllers. Propagation id: prop-9845.

incident-bot: Propagation event detected: prop-9845 -> region controllers ack: eu-west-2, ap-northeast-1, us-east-1.

Leah (duty-sre): Initiating edge route cache flush for affected routes. Command: `rbx route flush --region=ap-northeast-1 --prefixes=svc-gen-* --propagation=prop-9845`

Ravi (eng-runtime): Throttling background batch pipelines on eu-west-2: set concurrency=2 (was 8). Doing a graceful drain of queued KV caches to avoid double-miss.

Aisha (infra-oncall): After rollback and flush, p50 has dropped to ~210ms, error rate back to 0.5% for the pinned routes. Some clients still seeing 500s due to stale DNS caches.

Marco (netops): We've triggered a TCR (TTL cache re-key) for edge resolvers: `dnsctl evict --zone=redwood-cloud.net --name=*.edge.redwood-cloud.net --force` — this should accelerate client re-resolution. Note: it may take up to 2 TTL cycles for some ISPs.

Julia (support-lead): Notifying impacted customers with status update: initial mitigation applied, rollback in progress, potential transient errors for 5-20m. Internal postmortem will follow.

customer-advocate: Posted update to customers: "We're seeing a routing policy regression that briefly increased latency and errors for some cross-region requests. We've reverted the policy change and are monitoring; normal service expected shortly."

Leah (duty-sre): Monitoring metrics: steering decision fairness, route weights, edge latency, 5xx rate. Adding a temporary alert if p50 > 400ms or 5xx > 1% for next 30m.

incident-bot: Pager: oncall escalation timeout at 03:40 UTC if unresolved.

Aisha (infra-oncall): Handing off to next on-call for long-tail validation. @Leah, take it for the 03:45-07:45 window; I'll stay available for questions.

Leah (duty-sre): Ack. I'll keep the monitoring window and will coordinate rollback verification with Marco.

Marco (netops): Post-rollback validation: sampling shows 98.7% of routes now using intended weights. No config drift detected. Will run a dry-run for the smoothing window change in staging with extended canary before reapplying.

Ravi (eng-runtime): Runtime note: we saw a small increase in cold-KV misses after flush (~2.1% to 4.6%) — expected; warmed caches are recovering. No CPU/GPU saturation.

Julia (support-lead): Support ticket updates sent to affected orgs. No escalations to sales yet.

Aisha (infra-oncall): Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 at 03:38 UTC (mitigated, monitoring). Full postmortem required because change didn't go through proper canary gates.

incident-bot: Incident RE-INF-2026-4721 status: mitigated -> SEV3. Postmortem assigned to Marco + Ravi + Aisha. Due in 72h.

customer-advocate: Suggested postmortem action items: 1) enforce canary gate for smoothing-window changes, 2) add a precommit validation to detect abrupt weight deltas, 3) update runbook to include DNS evict steps for cross-region failovers.

Leah (duty-sre): Oncall handoff note: I'll monitor for 2hr window then escalate if regression. Leaving ephemeral logs at /var/logs/incident/RE-INF-2026-4721.log for 7d.

Aisha (infra-oncall): Thanks team. Closing active page. If anything pops back up ping me directly. :thumbsup:
